questions.title: Ball Hits a Power Line Above the Fairway
questions.question: You hit your shot from the tee and your ball bounces off a power line above the fairway and lands in the rough. What should you do?

choices.text: You always have to hit your shot again.
You always play the ball from where it stops.
It depends. If the course says you must replay the shot if this happens, then you do. If not, you play the ball from where it stops.
You add a one-shot penalty and play the ball from where it stopped.

questions.explanation: If your ball hits a power line above the course, you don't always have to replay. Some courses have a special rule that says you must hit again if this happens. If they do, you repeat your shot with no penalty. If not, you just play your ball from where it landed. Always read the course rules first.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Wires held up by poles that bring electricity and sometimes run high above the golf course.
The neatly cut grass that you aim for after your tee shot.
A special rule made by the golf course that players must follow there.

questions.teachingTip: Remind your players to always look at the scorecard or rules notice at the course to see if there are any Local Rules before teeing off.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids might think you always replay the shot if you hit a power line.
Some might believe you always have to play the ball from where it lands.
Sometimes kids might think there's always a penalty for hitting a power line.

questions.title: Ball Strikes Overhead Power Line
questions.question: Your tee shot strikes an overhead power line stretching across the fairway before bouncing into the rough. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: You must always replay the stroke.
You always play the ball as it lies.
It depends. If the Committee has adopted a Local Rule requiring a replay, you must replay the stroke. Otherwise, you play the ball as it lies.
You receive a one-stroke penalty and play the ball from where it finished.

questions.explanation: There is no Rule of Golf that automatically requires a stroke to be replayed after a ball hits an overhead power line or cable. However, many golf courses adopt Model Local Rule E-11, which requires a player to cancel the stroke and replay it if the ball hits a specified power line or supporting structure. If no such Local Rule is in force, the ball is played as it lies after striking the power line. Always check the Local Rules before starting your round.
